findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The PIC stated a cooler has not been obtained. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 6/29/26. Contact the inspector as soon as the new cooling unit has been obtained to verify proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The animal proteins stored in the single standing cooler (cottage cheese, whipped cream cheese, and milk) were observed to have internal temperatures between 49-55F. CORRECTED- the milk was stated to have been placed in the cooler within the past 2 hours, and was placed in a working cooler. The cottage cheese and whipped cream cheeses were stated to have been in the unit since Friday, and were voluntarily discarded. Ensure all animal proteins, cut tomatoes and melons, and items labeled “keep refrigerated” are kept at 41F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The standing cooler at the kitchen entry was observed to have an ambient temperature of 50F. Staff stated the cooler was repaired last week, and observed to have been working for 3 days. A bid for a new cooling unit has been placed. Do not place (temperature control for food safety) TCS foods in the unit until ambient temperatures are 41F or below. Inspector suggests keeping logs for the temperatures of the cooling units. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 6/18/27 to verify compliance.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspector observed 3 cans of food (mushrooms X2 and green beans) to contain significant dents along the seams. CORRECTED- cans were segregated from those for service to be returned to food supplier for credit. Ensure hermetically sealed cans are inspected for dents along the seams, and large dents along the body while stocking dry storage. Cans that are dented along the seams may allow for the entry and harborage of Botulism.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.[Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: The sanitizer bucket used for wiping food contact surfaces was observed to have no measurable sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- The bucket was remade to 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are made at a frequency to hold the concentration as recommended by the manufacterer's label (200-400 ppm quaternary ammonia).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The gallons of milk in the single standing cooler at the kitchen’s entry were probed to have an internal temperatures between 48-50F. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) stated the milk had been delivered the previous day, so the milk (9 gallons) was discarded. A prune juice that was opened to take measure its internal temperature (labeled “refrigerate after opening”) was moved to the working 3 door cooler. Ensure all animal proteins, cut tomatoes and melons, and items labeled “keep refrigerated” are kept at 41F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- Inspector observed opened milk, cut tomatoes, and prepared salads to lack date marking. CORRECTED- items were opened or prepared the previous day, and marked with the corresponding date. Ensure all ready to eat, temperature control for food safety (TCS) items are marked with a date after preparation/ thawing/ opening, to be used or discarded within seven days to prevent the growth and harborage of Listeria. The day of opening/ thawing/ preparation counts as day one.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an open gallon of milk with a 5/24 expiration date in the memory care refrigerator. CORRECTED- the milk was discarded. Ensure milk is DATE MARKED once opened, to be used or discarded within seven days of date marking, OR by the expiration date, whichever comes first.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The standing single cooler at the kitchen’s entry was observed to have an ambient temperature of approximately 50F. The PIC stated the unit had been serviced approximately two weeks ago. At this time, the unit is failing to hold TCS foods at or below 41F- see violation #22. Ensure the unit is serviced or repaired by 6/8/26 to hold TCS foods at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: The ambient thermometer in the kitchen’s standing cooler was observed to be broken. CORRECTED- the thermometer was replaced with a new working thermometer, and placed towards the front of the unit. Ensure cooling units contain working ambient thermometers to monitor temperatures of cooling units to be at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 4-502.11(B) Good Repair and Calibration. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. [Pf]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed 3 boxes of canned foods stored on the floor of dry storage. Ensure all food and food contact surfaces are stored at least 6 inches above the ground to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed forks, spoons, and knives in Memory Care stored with food contact surfaces facing UPWARDS. CORRECTED- the utensils were rearranged with a gloved hand so that only the hand contact surfaces were available to be dispensed. Ensure food contact surfaces are stored in a manner to prevent potential bare hand or environmental contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the top of the dish machine to contain a significant accumulation of debris. Nonfood contact surfaces should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris. Nonfood contact surfaces that contain debris may contaminate food contact surfaces. Increase the frequency at which this surfaces is cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment: No designated person in charge (PIC) was present during the majority of today’s inspection. The kitchen was left unattended for a short period of time, during which time a resident or guest could have entered the kitchen and contaminated food intended for service. During today’s inspection multiple priority and priority foundation violations were cited. These violations include, but are not limited to, no date marking, improper hand washing and times to wash hands, improper concentration of sanitizer and lack of education regarding use of sanitizer. The inspector will return on 02/12/26 to ensure all priority and priority foundation violations have been corrected.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection. [Pf]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There was no Certified Food Protection Manager (CFM/CFPM) present during the majority of today’s inspection. CORRECTED- a CFM arrived towards the end of the inspection. The presence of a CFM oversees and educates staff on safe food handling practices, and helps reduce the incidence of food-borne illnesses. Ensure a CFM is present during ALL times at which food is being handled or prepared.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed multiple incidents of food handlers switching tasks and donning gloves without handwashing. CORRECTED- Education was conducted with the PIC regarding appropriate times to wash hands per the food code. Review times to wash hands with all staff who handle food.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) [P].

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a food handler wash hands, and then turn off the faucet without the use of a barrier. CORRECTED- education about the importance of a barrier was provided and the individual rewashed their hands, using a barrier to turn off the faucet. Ensure all food handlers use a clean barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid recontaminating hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a dish in the basin of the sink in the Memory Care kitchenette. CORRECTED- the dish was removed from the basin and education about hand washing sink usage was provided. The PIC stated that all dishes are to be brought back to the main kitchen for ware washing. Ensure hand washing sinks are used for hand washing ONLY, so as not to deter frequent hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Multiple food contact surfaces were observed to contain an accumulation of soil debris:
1) The food contact surface (blade) of the facility’s can opener. CORRECTED-the can opened was pulled to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized
2) The internal surfaces and the baffles of the ice machine contain soil debris and limescale. Inspector will return on 02/12/26 to check that the ice machine has been cleaned and sanitized.
Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer bucket used for wiping food contact surfaces was observed to have no measurable sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- The bucket was remade to 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. The staff member was making a sanitizer bucket from an incorrect dispenser, and education was provided. Ensure ongoing education about the proper use of sanitizers occurs frequently.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no date marking within the facility. CORRECTED- the PIC applied dates to food opened or prepared within the past seven days. Food that had an unknown date or preparation, or that was prepared over seven days ago was voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Education was provided regarding which items should be date marked. This violation will be spot checked during the 02/12/26 reinspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspector observed two probe thermometers to be out of calibration. CORRECTED- the inspector demonstrated how to calibrate a stem thermometer using the ice water method. Both thermometers were calibrated during today’s inspection. Ensure stem thermometers are maintained in good repair to check proper internal cooking temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-502.11(B) Good Repair and Calibration. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. [Pf]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspector observed 6 cans of green beans stored on the floor of dry storage. Ensure all food and food contact surfaces are stored at least 6 inches above the ground to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple food contact surfaces to be in improper storage:
1) Forks and spoons in Memory Care were stored with a mixed orientation. CORRECTED- the utensils were rearranged with a gloved hand so that only the hand contact surfaces were available to be dispensed.
2) Plates in the kitchen were stored with an exposed food contact surface. Plates should be inverted or stored under a covering during storage.
Ensure food contact surfaces are stored in a manner to prevent potential bare hand or environmental contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the handle of the single standing cooler in the kitchen to be deteriorated and contain duct tape to hold it in place. All nonfood contact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure equipment is repaired or replaced by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the facility’s heat measuring dish puck to be nonoperational. Inspector will return on 02/12/26 to ensure the heat registering dish puck is working to verify proper sanitizing temperatures for heat sanitizing dish machine.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.13(A) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple drawers storing food utensils to contain debris. Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT: Two damp mop heads were observed stored in the basin of the mop sink and mop bucket during today’s inspection. CORRECTED- the PIC moved to the mops to the top of the mop buckets, so that they may air dry. Ensure mops are stored in a position that allows for air drying moving forward.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Caulking is missing behind triple sink to the right of the dish machine. Areas that are not easily moved for cleaning must be sealed to the wall. Seal the space between the wall and the sink prior to next routine inspection to prevent the entry and harborage of mold and bacteria with a high water activity.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple incidents of food handlers donning gloves without washing hands. CORRECTED- Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that hands are washed at each time that it is required per code. Ensure that hand washing takes place prior to donning gloves in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) [P].

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Hand sink in Memory Care was lacking paper towels. CORRECTED- PIC resupplied hand sink. All hand sinks must be supplied with paper towels at all times.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel. [Pf].

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment:
REPEAT
Numerous dented cans were observed throughout the dry storage area. Ensure cans that are dented along the top, bottom, or side seams are discarded, as are any cans with significant dents that create sharp edges. CORRECTED- Dented cans were pulled aside to be returned to the supplier or voluntarily discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
1) Two knives on the magnetic knife strip were observed to have food debris on them. 
2) Scoop holder for ice machine was observed to contain floating debris.

Utensils and utensil holder were pulled to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned after each use and are maintained clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

REPEAT
Food debris or soil accumulation was observed under the 3 door cooler and freezer. Discussed with PIC the need to clean under equipment. Ensure facility is cleaned at a frequency to avoid accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

REPEAT
Damp mop heads were observed stored in the basin of the mop sink. Education was provided to PIC about proper mop storage to prevent growth of bacteria. Ensure mops are stored correctly between uses moving forward.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

Both utensils were pulled to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Ensure utensils are cleaned after each use and are maintained clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Several rubber spatulas were observed to be cracked or damaged. CORRECTED- Spatula were pulled from use to be discarded. Discard utensils as they become damaged and are no longer easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.11 Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: 2nd REPEAT: No sanitizer bucket was prepared upon inspectors arrival during breakfast clean up and while an employee began food preparations for lunch. CORRECTED- Upon request, employee prepared a sanitizer bucket, which was observed at 400 ppm quat.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11 (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [Pf]

findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.comment:
1) Damp or molded mop heads were observed stored in the basin of the mop sink. 
2) Two mop buckets were observed containing dirty mop water. Discard molded mop heads and store others where they will air-dry after use. Discard mop water promptly after use.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Caulking is damaged or missing along the edge of the sprayer sink/drainboard to the left of the dish machine. Repair or replace seal between the drainboard and the wall.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Lightbulbs in the kitchen and dish area were observed without shields or protective covers. Provide shields/covers over lightbulbs.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.11 (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, light bulbs shall be shielded, coated, or otherwise shatter-resistant in areas where there is exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; or unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Lighting is dim and blinking in the dish area. Provide sufficient lighting in the dish area.
findings.citation_text: 6-303.11 The light intensity shall be: (C) At least 540 lux (50 foot candles) at a surface where a FOOD EMPLOYEE is working with FOOD or working with UTENSILS or EQUIPMENT such as knives, slicers, grinders, or saws where EMPLOYEE safety is a factor. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
1) 1st REPEAT: Soil accumulation was observed on the blade of the can opener. CORRECTED- Can opener was removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized.
2) Mold accumulation was observed on the interior of the ice machine. Clean and sanitize the ice machine as frequently as needed to prevent mold accumulation. CORRECTED- PIC cleaned and sanitized the ice machine.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Yogurt, liquid eggs, and shell eggs were observed at 58-60F after being stored on the countertop through breakfast service. CORRECTED- Out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded. Discussed creating a time as a control policy, or using the probe thermometer to check temperatures before returning foods to the cooler after storage on the countertop. See General Comments for additional information.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
In the 3 door cooler, tuna and marinara sauce were observed without date labels. A container of ham was observed dated 10/10/24, presumed to be the discard date. This is inconsistent with the facility’s standard date-marking practice to label with the date opened/prepared. CORRECTED- Two containers of tuna and one container of ham were voluntarily discarded. Ensure foods are labeled using a consistent date-marking system to ensure foods are used or discarded within 7 days of opening or preparation.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: There was no sanitizer solution prepared in the kitchen during breakfast service. Keep sanitizer buckets prepared and available during all times of food prep, service, and clean up. PIC prepared a sanitizer bucket upon request, which was observed at 200ppm quat.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11 (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Food debris was observed in the bottom of the 3 door cooler. Clean non-food contact surfaces as often as necessary to prevent soil accumulation.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Dirty mop water was observed a mop bucket from the previous night. Ensure used mop water is discarded after use.
6-501.114: The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
1) Food employee observed using a cellphone, then handling clean dishes without washing hands first.
2) Food employee observed entering the kitchen, handling clean dishes, handling dirty dishes, then returning to clean dishes without washing hands at any point.
CORRECTED- Discussed handwashing with PIC, who will review handwashing with food employees. Employees must wash hands upon entering the kitchen and after any task that may have contaminated hands (such as handling a cellphone or dirty dishes). 
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Soil accumulation was observed on the blade of the can opener. CORRECTED- A new can opener has already been purchased. The current can opener will be removed and replaced.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
The ambient thermometer in the 3 door cooler was found to be broken. Ensure all cold holding units have functional ambient thermometers inside.
4-204.112: (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. [C]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Several wet wiping cloths were observed on the kitchen countertops. Wet wiping cloths must be stored submerged in sanitizer solution.
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. [C]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
The ice scoop was observed stored on a cloth above the ice machine. In-use utensils must be stored with the handle extending out of the food or on a clean surface (such as in a pan or on a tray that is regularly washed, rinsed, and sanitized). CORRECTED- PIC provided a plastic bucket to store the ice scoop.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: There was no sanitizer solution prepared in the kitchen during post-lunch clean up. Keep sanitizer buckets prepared and available during all times of food prep, service, and clean up. PIC prepared a sanitizer bucket upon request, which was observed at 200ppm quat.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11 (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [C]
